tb-E401-1.question:
Chris is suffering from short-sightedness and his uncorrected far point is at 2 m from the eye. Find the power of the spectacles required to correct the defect.

A –0.5 D

B +0.5 D

C –2.0 D

D +2.0 D
tb-E401-1.reasoning:
An object at the corrected far point (u = ∞) forms an image on the uncorrected far point (v = −2 m) by the spectacles (P = ?).

P = 1u + 1v = 1∞ + 1-2 = −0.5 D

tb-E401-6.question:
Which of the following statements about a lens with a power of –10 D is/are correct?

(1) It is a concave lens.

(2) Its focal length is 10 cm.

(3) It bends light more than a lens with a power of –5 D.

A (2) only

B (1) and (2) only

C (1) and (3) only

D (1), (2) and (3)
tb-E401-6.reasoning:
A lens with a negative power is a concave lens.

∴ (1) is correct.

f = 1P = 1-10 = −0.1 m (−10 cm)

The focal length of the lens is 10 cm.

∴ (2) is correct.

A lens with a power of larger magnitude bends light more.

∴ (3) is correct.

tb-E401-7.question:
The far point of an eye is at infinity. If the powers of the eye are +41 D and +38 D when looking at an object at its near point and far point respectively, how far is the near point from the eye?

A 25 cm

B 28.5 cm

C 30.3 cm

D 33.3 cm
tb-E401-7.reasoning:
An object at the far point (u = ∞) forms an image on the retina (v = ?) by the eye (P = +38 D).

P = 1u + 1v

38 = 1∞ + 1v

v = 0.02632 m

An object at the near point (u = ?) forms an image on the retina (v = 0.02632 m) by the eye (P = +41 D).

P = 1u + 1v

41 = 1u + 10.02632

u = 0.333 m

The near point is 0.333 m (33.3 cm) from the eye.

source.name: E401 Revision 1 Human Vision and Fibre Optic Endoscopy.docx

tb-E401-8.question:
Betty is wearing concave spectacles with a power of –1.25 D. The range of accommodation of her eye without the spectacles is from 25 cm to 80 cm. Find the range of accommodation of her eye with the spectacles.

A From 28.3 cm to 80 cm

B From 28.3 cm to infinity

C From 36.4 cm to 80 cm

D From 36.4 cm to infinity
tb-E401-8.reasoning:
An object at the near point after wearing the spectacles (u = ?) forms an image on the original near point (v = −0.25 m) by the spectacles (P = −1.25 D).

P = 1u + 1v

−1.25 = 1u + 1-0.25

u = 0.364 m (36.4 cm)

An object at the far point after wearing the spectacles (u = ?) forms an image on the original far point (v = −0.8 m) by the spectacles (P = −1.25 D).

P = 1u + 1v

−1.25 = 1u + 1-0.8

1u = 0

u = ∞

The range of accommodation of her eye with the spectacles is from 36.4 cm to infinity.

source.name: E401 Revision 1 Human Vision and Fibre Optic Endoscopy.docx

tb-E401-9.question:
Figure d shows a smiley face formed by small blue dots reflecting light of wavelength 450 nm. The distance between adjacent blue dots forming the outline of the face is 1 mm. Jack looks at the picture from a distance d. He sees the face without realizing that its outline is formed by small blue dots. Given that the diameter of his pupil is 2 mm, find the minimum value of d.

A 1 mm

B 2 mm

C 1.82 m

D 3.64 m
tb-E401-9.reasoning:
θR ≈ 1.22λd = 1.22×(450×10-9)0.002 = 2.745 × 10−4 rad

By θ ≈ xu,

u ≈ xθ = 0.0012.745×10-4 = 3.64 m

The minimum value of d is 3.64 m.

source.name: E401 Revision 1 Human Vision and Fibre Optic Endoscopy.docx

tb-E401-18.question:
Karen is looking at a card board with red light passing through the slits on it. Each slit is separated by 1 mm (Fig i). The wavelength of red light is 680 nm. The diameter of the pupil of Karen’s eye is 6 mm.

(a) Estimate the minimum angular separation of two slits so that they can be resolved by Karen’s eye. (2 marks)

(b) How far should the card board be placed from Karen so that she can just distinguish each slit? (2 marks)

(c) Assume the card board is placed as the distance in (b). Karen thinks that she can still distinguish each slit if the red light is replaced by a violet light. Is she correct? Explain briefly. (3 marks)
tb-E401-18.answer:
(a) θR ≈ 1.22λd = 1.22×(680×10-9)0.006 1M

= 1.383 × 10−4 rad

≈ 1.38 × 10−4 rad 1A

(b) By θ ≈ xu,

u ≈ xθ = 0.0011.383×10-4 1M

= 7.23 m 1A

The card board should be placed at 7.23 m from Karen so that she can just distinguish each slit.

(c) She is correct. 1A

Violet light has shorter wavelengths λ than red light. 1A

By θR ≈ 1.22λd, replacing the red light by a violet light would reduce θR. 1A

tb-E401-19.question:
Tom is suffering from long-sightedness. The power of his eye is +40 D when looking at an object at infinity.

(a) Find the distance between the retina and the optical centre of the refracting parts of Tom’s eye. (2 marks)

(b) Tom wears a pair of convex lenses with a power of +3 D and the near-point distance of his eye with the lenses is at 25 cm.

(i) Does a high-power lens or low-power lens bend light more? (1 mark)

(ii) Find the effective power of the combination of his eye and the convex lenses when he is looking at an object at 25 cm. (2 marks)

(iii) Find the near-point distance of Tom’s eye without the lenses. (2 marks)

(c) Both long-sightedness and old-sightedness lead to problems with near vision. Compare the causes of these two defects of vision. (2 marks)
tb-E401-19.answer:
(a) P = 1u + 1v

40 = 1∞ + 1v 1M

v = 0.025 m 1A

The distance between the retina and the optical centre of the refracting parts of Tom’s eye is 0.025 m.

(b) (i) A high-power lens 1A

(ii) Effective power

= 1u + 1v

= 10.25 + 10.025 1M

= +44 D 1A

(iii) An object at the corrected near point (u = 0.25 m) forms an image at the uncorrected near point (v = ?) by the convex lenses (P = +3 D).

P = 1u + 1v

3 = 10.25 + 1v 1M

v = −1 m

The near-point distance of Tom’s eye without the lenses is 1 m. 1A

(c) A person suffers from long-sightedness when the eyeball is too short, or the lens is too thin when the ciliary muscles contract maximally. 1A

A person suffers from old-sightedness when the elasticity of lens decreases due to ageing. 1A

tb-E401-21.question:
An endoscope uses a coherent bundle to transmit images and an incoherent bundle to transmit light for illumination.

(a) With the aid of a diagram, describe what a coherent bundle is and explain how it transmits images. (3 marks)

(b) Tommy thinks that the endoscope can still function normally if the incoherent bundle is also replaced by another coherent bundle. Is he correct? Explain briefly. (2 marks)

(c) It is known that the critical angle at the core-cladding interface of an optical fibre is 65°. Find the ratio of the refractive index of the core to that of the cladding. (2 marks)
tb-E401-21.answer:
(a)

(Correct diagram) 1A

A coherent bundle is a bundle of optical fibres manufactured in a way that the relative positions of the optical fibres are preserved from one end to the other. 1A

This maintenance of position allows an image at one end to be reproduced faithfully at the other end. 1A

(b) He is correct. 1A

A coherent bundle can also transmit light. 1A

(c) By Snell’s law,

n1 sin θ1 = n2 sin θ2

n1 sin 65° = n2 sin 90° 1M

n1n2 = 1.10

The ratio of the refractive index of the core to that of the cladding is 1.10 : 1. 1A

tb-E401-22.answer:

(ii) At 32 cm 1A

(b)

(Light rays converge to somewhere in front of the retina) 1A

(Light rays converge to somewhere behind the retina) 1A

(c) (i) An object at the corrected near point (u = ?) forms an image on the uncorrected near point (v = −0.32 m) by the spectacles (P = +0.875 D).
